newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rice exporters keen to clinch Iraq deal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rice exporters keen to clinch Iraq deal.

text.p: Pakistani exporters said on Wednesday they hoped to sell around 500,000 tonnes of IRRI-6 rice to Iraq but expected tough competition from India.
"We expect to have an exportable surplus of 700,000 tonnes of IRRI-6, out of which we can export at least 500,000 tonnes to Iraq," Khalid Ghori of Macto Rice Processing Ltd said.
He said Iraq was likely to be in the market for more than a million tonnes of rice for 1997.
Jordanian traders said on Tuesday that Iraq had unfrozen $70 million of funds in a deal arranged by an Austrian firm in exchange for substantial commodity purchases.

Exporters say two Pakistani firms won tenders to supply 41,800 tonnes of IRRI-6 rice to the Grain Board of Iraq last month. Nabil Enterprises Ltd was to export 15,000 tonnes at $238 per tonne CIF for shipment to Um Qasr port by December 15. Mahmood (pvt) Ltd was to ship 26,800 tonnes at $239.74 CIF by the last week of November.

The Grain Board called for the tender through the Pakistani embassy in Baghdad, after clearance from the U.N. sanctions committee, following a deal signed with the Pakistan government on October 6 to supply foodstuffs and other commodities to Iraq.
Exporters said at the time that the deals had yet to be finalised as the two governments had to work out the mode of payment. "We expect the matter to be cleared now," Ghori said.
According to exporters, India was said to be seeking a big rice deal with Iraq, which usually meets most of its needs from Pakistan, Vietnam and Thailand.

"Thailand is expensive while Vietnam is unlikely to match quality. It only leaves Pakistan and India in the field," Ghori said, adding that a recent fall in the domestic prices of IRRI-6 was likely to make Pakistani exports more competitive.
"We expect domestic rates to fall as low as $195 per tonne giving us room to export at current FOB rates of $215 per tonne," he said.
Pakistan's rice output is likely to reach 3.5 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July-June), slightly up on last year's 3.47 million.
Production of IRRI-6 is estimated at 2.27 million tonnes and superior quality basmati at 1.2 million.
